hub.title: Attitude
hub.subtitle: Diagnose what's holding you back so you can lead from your strengths.

saboteurCard.heading: Mental Fitness Assessment
saboteurCard.body: 10 minutes — 50 statements + 24 emotion pairs. Reveal your top saboteurs, your PQ score, and the Sage Powers that counter them.

intro.heading: One sharper view of yourself.
intro.body: You'll rate 50 short statements (how often each is true for you) and then choose between 24 pairs of feelings. There are no right answers — go with your first instinct.

saboteurStep.title: Saboteur statements
saboteurStep.instructions: Rate how often each statement is true for you right now.

pqStep.title: Emotion pairs
pqStep.instructions: For each pair, rate how strongly you feel each side right now.

navigation.completeRequired: Answer all questions on this page to continue.

result.title: Your Saboteur Profile
result.pqHint: PQ measures the ratio between your Sage (constructive) and Saboteur (sabotaging) mental responses. PQ ≥ 75 is the tipping point for sustained performance and wellbeing.
result.radarHint: How much each of the 10 saboteurs shows up in your responses (0-10).
result.exploreOthersHint: Click any saboteur to read about it. Self-knowledge of the patterns you don't lead with is what keeps them from sneaking in later.

critical.label: Saboteurs dominate
critical.description: Your saboteurs control most of your responses right now. This isn't a judgment — it's a starting point. The good news: improvement is fastest when the gap is widest.

mixed.label: Mixed zone
mixed.description: Sage and saboteurs split control roughly evenly. Under stress, saboteurs take over. Big room to grow.

good.label: Near the tipping point
good.description: Your Sage is showing up, but saboteurs still hijack important moments. With consistent practice you can cross 75 in a few weeks.

excellent.label: Above the tipping point
excellent.description: You've crossed PQ 75. Sage runs most of the show. Saboteurs exist but no longer dominate. You're reaping the benefits of mental fitness.

mastery.label: Excellent mental fitness
mastery.description: Your Sage is firmly in command. You meet challenges with calm, clarity, and constructive energy. Keep the practice up.

judge.name: The Judge
judge.tagline: Universal saboteur — runs background commentary against yourself, others, and circumstances.
judge.origin: Formed early as a survival mechanism — vigilance against threat. The voice grew up with you and never stopped narrating.
judge.sageAntidote: Empathize with yourself first, then with what's actually happening.

stickler.name: The Stickler
stickler.tagline: Demands perfection from self and others. Misses the 80% that's already good enough.
stickler.origin: Praise for being 'the responsible one'. Mistakes were costly. Order felt like safety.
stickler.sageAntidote: Navigate by what truly matters, not what merely needs to be perfect.

pleaser.name: The Pleaser
pleaser.tagline: Wins approval by serving others — until resentment leaks through the smile.
pleaser.origin: Love felt conditional. You learned that being useful kept people close.
pleaser.sageAntidote: Empathize with your own needs, then activate from a real choice.

hyperAchiever.name: The Hyper-Achiever
hyperAchiever.tagline: Identity fused to results. The next win never quite lasts.
hyperAchiever.origin: Approval came with achievement. Stillness felt unsafe.
hyperAchiever.sageAntidote: Navigate from values, not scoreboards. Empathize with the part that just wants to be enough.

victim.name: The Victim
victim.motto: Why does this happen to me?
victim.tagline: Pulls sympathy through suffering. Stays stuck because being stuck is familiar.
victim.origin: Care came mostly when you were unwell or distressed.
victim.sageAntidote: Activate the smallest possible action. Empathize without merging with the pain.

hyperRational.name: The Hyper-Rational
hyperRational.tagline: Treats feelings as inefficient. Comes across cold; misses what's really going on.
hyperRational.origin: Emotions were dismissed or punished. Logic kept you safe.
hyperRational.sageAntidote: Empathize first. Then explore what the data of feeling reveals.

hyperVigilant.name: The Hyper-Vigilant
hyperVigilant.tagline: Scans for threats even when things are fine. Cynicism as armor.
hyperVigilant.origin: Reality was unpredictable. Hyper-alertness reduced harm.
hyperVigilant.sageAntidote: Navigate toward what matters, not away from what scares you.

restless.name: The Restless
restless.tagline: Boredom is unbearable, presence is hard. Always chasing the next stimulus.
restless.origin: Stillness felt like emptiness or danger. Stimulation became identity.
restless.sageAntidote: Explore deeply where you are before chasing the next thing.

controller.name: The Controller
controller.tagline: Loss of control = anxiety. Pushes others; pushes self twice as hard.
controller.origin: Chaos felt unsafe. Taking charge protected you and others.
controller.sageAntidote: Empathize with your need for control, then navigate by trust.

avoider.name: The Avoider
avoider.tagline: Side-steps conflict, hard conversations, and unpleasant truths. Calls it 'staying positive.'
avoider.origin: Conflict was punished or dangerous. Avoidance kept the peace.
avoider.sageAntidote: Activate the smallest courageous step. Empathize with what you'd rather not see.

empathize.name: Empathize
empathize.description: Approach yourself, others, and the situation with curiosity and care rather than judgment. Empathy disarms most saboteurs at the root.

explore.name: Explore
explore.description: Open up to what's true without rushing to conclude or react. Useful before any decision or hard conversation.

innovate.name: Innovate
innovate.description: Generate non-obvious options. Break the binary 'either/or' that saboteurs love.

navigate.name: Navigate
navigate.description: Pause and ask what truly matters here, then choose accordingly. Cuts through perfectionism and reactivity.

activate.name: Activate
activate.description: Commit and move — laser-focused on the most useful next step. Counters paralysis, pleasing, and avoidance.

questions.sab_j01: I criticize myself harshly for my mistakes, even small ones.
questions.sab_j02: I'm rarely satisfied with my own results, even when others appreciate them.
questions.sab_j03: I blame myself for things that happened a long time ago.
questions.sab_j04: I tend to focus on what's wrong with people rather than their strengths.
questions.sab_j05: I often judge other people's choices as inferior to mine.
questions.sab_j06: When something goes wrong, my first reaction is to look for who's at fault.
questions.sab_j07: I often wake up at night worrying about things that might go wrong.
questions.sab_j08: When something isn't working, I struggle to see anything positive or opportunity in it.
questions.sab_s01: I get deeply frustrated when things aren't done the 'right' way.
questions.sab_s02: I spend more time than necessary perfecting details others wouldn't notice.
questions.sab_s03: I get irritated when others don't hold my standards of quality.
questions.sab_s04: I'd rather redo something myself than accept imperfect work from a colleague.
questions.sab_s05: The idea of 'good enough' makes me uncomfortable — things should be done well or not done.
questions.sab_p01: It's very hard for me to say 'no' to others' requests, even when I'm overloaded.
questions.sab_p02: I tend to put others' needs before my own, almost automatically.
questions.sab_p03: I feel hurt or resentful when others don't recognize how much I do for them.
questions.sab_p04: I try to earn people's affection through constant helpfulness and availability.
questions.sab_p05: I feel guilty when I spend time only on myself.
questions.sab_ha01: My self-worth depends heavily on my professional results.
questions.sab_ha02: After a success, I quickly move to the next goal without letting myself celebrate.
questions.sab_ha03: I feel uncomfortable or guilty when I'm not doing something 'productive'.
questions.sab_ha04: I tend to evaluate people's worth (including my own) by their achievements.
questions.sab_ha05: I worry that without constant, visible success, people would respect me less.
questions.sab_v01: I often feel bad things happen to me more than to others.
questions.sab_v02: Sometimes I dwell on my problems so others show me sympathy and understanding.
questions.sab_v03: I feel powerless against the circumstances in my life, as if I can't change them.
questions.sab_v04: I tend to complain about how things aren't fair to me.
questions.sab_hr01: I tend to process everything through logic and analysis, including personal relationships.
questions.sab_hr02: I get impatient when people are led by emotions instead of facts.
questions.sab_hr03: I prefer to analyze a problem rather than talk about how it makes me feel.
questions.sab_hr04: Others have told me I sometimes seem cold or emotionally detached.
questions.sab_hv01: I worry constantly about what could go wrong, even when things are going well.
questions.sab_hv02: I struggle to trust other people's real intentions.
questions.sab_hv03: I find reassurance in rules, procedures, and authority figures.
questions.sab_hv04: When things go well, part of me waits for something bad to happen.
questions.sab_hv05: I'm often cynical or skeptical about people's motives.
questions.sab_r01: I get bored easily and constantly seek new stimuli or activities.
questions.sab_r02: I have a hard time sitting still and enjoying the present moment.
questions.sab_r03: I'm easily distracted and tend to jump between activities without finishing them.
questions.sab_r04: I'm afraid of missing out on experiences or opportunities (FOMO).
questions.sab_c01: I feel a strong need to be in control of situations and the people around me.
questions.sab_c02: I feel intense anxiety when I can't influence or determine the outcome of something.
questions.sab_c03: I tend to tell others what to do and how, even when not asked.
questions.sab_c04: I find it very hard to delegate because I think I'd do it better.
questions.sab_c05: When I'm not in charge or don't have a say, I feel restless and anxious.
questions.sab_a01: I tend to postpone hard or uncomfortable conversations, hoping they'll resolve themselves.
questions.sab_a02: I prefer to focus on the positives of a situation rather than face the real issues.
questions.sab_a03: I have a hard time facing conflict directly — I'd rather avoid it.
questions.sab_a04: When stressed, I retreat into comforting routines or pleasant activities instead of addressing the cause.
questions.sab_a05: I often say 'everything's fine' even when it's not at all.
